verdict.rationale: Pulumi documents a DIY state backend that stores state in an object store the user manages (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage), and self-hosting is available. Together these let users control where their state data lives, but region or residency selection is only implied through the user's own storage choice. One community comment says Pulumi needs to call its hosted service and cannot run airgapped, and another notes self-hosting is Enterprise-only; both add caveats without directly contradicting the DIY backend docs. Missing for 10: explicit region/data-residency selection for the Pulumi Cloud managed backend, documentation framing backend choice as residency control, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)
